title.narrative: Protection, Care and Inclusion for Vulnerable Groups in Eastern Ukraine's

description.narrative: ltpgtThrough this project, VIS and implementing partner Genofond and the Salesian Congregation will seek to address critical needs and gaps in target locations through a two-fold strategy:ltbrgtthe primary objective is to enhance access to integrated healthcare in Dnipropetrovsk oblast focusing on Novomoskovskyi, Synelnykivskyi, and Nikopolskyi raions through the introduction of a Sensory Bus Mobile Unit. Manned by the Genofond multidisciplinary team, this unit targets early diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and referrals for children with special needs and disabilities, emphasizing interactive, corrective, and developmental interventions. Medical support and tailored rehabilitation, led by a pediatric neurologist, include prescription services and teleconsultations.ltbrgtA robust capacity-building program is integrated for the mobile team staff.ltbrgtSecondly, VIS and its IPs extend direct support in the same locations and additionally in Donetsk oblast (Kramatorsky and Pokrovsky Raions) and in the Kamyansk district of the Dnipropetrovsk region to vulnerable families, emphasizing the well-being and protection of conflict-affected children, their caregivers, and vulnerable community members. The VIS CP mobile team adopts a comprehensive approach, incorporating CP Case Management, customized family and dignity kits distribution, and psychological and psychosocial support. lt/pgtltpgtAdditionally, three barrier-free, safe Sensory Class are established in coordination with local authorities to facilitate inclusive education and serve as training venues for VIS and Genofund. lt/pgtltpgtTraining programs cover stress management, emotional resilience, disability inclusion, and self-care for various stakeholders, aiming to prevent burnout and ensure safety and inclusion. Local partner capacity building, mine awareness activities, and summer camps in Ternivka, Chumaky, Pershotravensk, Novodonetske, Kamianske and Pokrovsk (these are provided by the Salesian Congregation) complement the initiative, offering a comprehensive approach to child protection capacity building, with a focus on emotional well-being and safety in targeted communities.ltbrgt Overall, the project will reach 10332 individuals including (2479 women, 3016 girls, 1883 men, and 2954 boys).ltbrgtlt/pgt
